\section[o risco]{o risco — the risk; the line, the scratch}

\label{lesson:PT-C373-risco}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for final, then the Portuguese for flexible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o risco}
\textbf{o risco} — \textquotedblleft{}the risk; the line, the scratch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não quero correr o risco de perder o comboio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not want to run the risk of missing the train.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Correr o risco} — to run the risk. Also a line or a scratch: \emph{um risco no carro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{risco} \textquotedblleft{}risk\textquotedblright{} is not settled; it goes with Italian \emph{rischio} and Spanish \emph{riesgo}, while \emph{risco} \textquotedblleft{}line, scratch\textquotedblright{} belongs with the verb \emph{riscar} \textquotedblleft{}to scratch\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists \emph{risco} \textquotedblleft{}line\textquotedblright{}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o risco}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o risco}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o risco}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for final, then the Portuguese for flexible, then say \emph{o risco} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o risco mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The risk; the line, the scratch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[arriscado]{arriscado — risky}

\label{lesson:PT-C373-arriscado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for flexible, then the Portuguese for the risk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: arriscado}
\textbf{arriscado} — \textquotedblleft{}risky\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Atravessar a rua com o semáforo vermelho é arriscado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Crossing the street on a red light is risky.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{arriscar} — to risk.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{arriscado} is the participle of \emph{arriscar} \textquotedblleft{}to risk\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB analyses as \emph{a-} + \emph{risco} + \emph{-ar} (EtymDB); the origin of \emph{risco} \textquotedblleft{}risk\textquotedblright{} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for flexible, then the Portuguese for the risk, then say \emph{arriscado} again

\section[provável]{provável — likely, probable}

\label{lesson:PT-C373-provavel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the risk, then the Portuguese for risky.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: provável}
\textbf{provável} — \textquotedblleft{}likely, probable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
É provável que chova amanhã.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is likely to rain tomorrow.}
\end{quote}

\emph{É provável que} takes the subjunctive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{provável} comes from Latin \emph{probābilis} \textquotedblleft{}that may be believed or proved, likely\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{probāre} \textquotedblleft{}to test, to prove\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{provável}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{provável}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{provável}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the risk, then the Portuguese for risky, then say \emph{provável} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does provável mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Likely, probable\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[improvável]{improvável — unlikely, improbable}

\label{lesson:PT-C373-improvavel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for risky, then the Portuguese for likely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: improvável}
\textbf{improvável} — \textquotedblleft{}unlikely, improbable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
É improvável que ele mude de ideias.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is unlikely that he will change his mind.}
\end{quote}

\emph{É improvável que} takes the subjunctive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{improvável} comes from Latin \emph{improbābilis} \textquotedblleft{}not credible\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{probābilis} \textquotedblleft{}likely\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{probāre} \textquotedblleft{}to prove\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a probabilidade]{a probabilidade — the probability, the chance}

\label{lesson:PT-C373-probabilidade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for likely, then the Portuguese for unlikely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a probabilidade}
\textbf{a probabilidade} — \textquotedblleft{}the probability, the chance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Há uma grande probabilidade de nevar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is a good chance of snow.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Com toda a probabilidade} — in all likelihood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{probabilidade} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{probābilitās} \textquotedblleft{}probability, credibility\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{probābilis} \textquotedblleft{}likely\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{probāre} \textquotedblleft{}to prove\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
